label: W4A4 graphed decode
mechanism: the exp-0015a native FP4xFP4 grouped MMA extended to the routed experts INSIDE the exp-0012 CUDA-graphed decode step (bincount -> searchsorted makes the path capture-legal); after this no phase distinction is left in the routed-expert path
hypothesis: This is the second half of the exp-0015 split plan committed in DEADENDS; exp-0015a/0016 did prefill, this does decode. exp-0012's graphed-step kernel table — the current ground truth, since the step is GPU-bound after the dispatch floor was locked — puts the routed-expert GEMMs at 266.4 ms of the 322.7 ms decode step, running the W4A16 Triton kernel that pays the exp-0010 in-register convert-ALU floor (~2.5 cvt-class ops per weight element) on every weight tile. Native FP4 MMA deletes that pipe. BASE: 41e827e (exp-0016, in flight) merged with main, so this measures the COMBINATION of both halves rather than a stale disjoint half — the exp-0015a lesson recorded in exp-0016's own spec (git merge-base --is-ancestor main f09315b -> OK). ONE VARIABLE: model.py stops restricting the W4A4 kernel to phase=='prefill' (kill switch PYENGINE_W4A4_DECODE=0, read once at import like exp-0013's _FUSED_ATTN so captured graphs match eager warmups); moe_gemm_w4a4.py gets one capture-safety fix; plus two test files. Nothing else. CAPTURE BLOCKER FOUND AND FIXED EARLY, as the ruling demanded: torch.bincount is NOT graph-capturable — its CUDA path sizes the histogram from self.max().cpu(), and capture aborts with 'Cannot copy between CPU and CUDA tensors during CUDA graph capture' (t_w4a4_capture arm b, pre-fix). Replaced by a searchsorted boundary scan over 0..E on the already-sorted pair list: same exact integers, no sync, no atomics, and it subsumes the second cumsum. This does NOT perturb the accepted prefill path — offs/dst/src are the only outputs of the changed block and t_w4a4_decode arm a shows them BITWISE identical to the bincount form at T = 736/64/1/3000, so exp-0016's green D13 TF gate (parity_pass true, agree 379/400 = 0.9475, delta_mean 0.043856 vs bar 0.067851) transfers to this tree unchanged. LOCAL EVIDENCE (GPU 4, REAL layer-3 experts; /workspace/logs/t_w4a4_decode_exp0015b_out.log): (b) decode numerics WITH THE PREFILL-SHAPE CONTROL, which is the argument that matters — W4A4-vs-W4A16 at decode T=64 is rel_mean 1.934e0 / cos 0.98856, at the ACCEPTED prefill shape T=736 it is 1.901e0 / cos 0.98873, ratio 0.9998: decode W4A4 is the SAME numeric class as the already-accepted prefill W4A4, not a new risk (the full-chain rel_mean exceeds DEADENDS arm J's per-GEMM 9.5e-2 because two GEMMs, a silu, a routing epilogue and a 6-slot sum compound; being shape-invariant is the point); finite everywhere. (d) capture arms: capture+replay bitwise == eager, same-schedule determinism (two replays bitwise identical — the t_b3-adapted arm), and replay under a DIFFERENT routing bitwise == eager on that routing — load-bearing, since routing changes every step under a fixed graph, so the captured kernel must be a pure function of buffer contents; also validated at small shapes in t_w4a4_capture arms b/c/d. (e) speed, both paths CAPTURED and replayed on matched routing with the same weights: 11.197 ms/layer W4A16 -> 2.874 ms/layer W4A4 = 3.90x (3.70x on a prior run; the eager arm agrees at 3.79x). READ THE SPEED NUMBER CORRECTLY: the ABSOLUTE walls are on uniform-random routing, which hits 201/256 experts at T=64, and both kernels are per-hit-expert weight-traffic bound, so the trained router's concentration shrinks both sides in situ — which is exactly why W4A16 measures 11.2 ms/layer here against the in-situ table's 266.4/63 = 4.23 ms. The RATIO is the transferable quantity. RAGGED DECODE SEGMENTS (the flagged risk) are handled by construction and exercised: every expert group is padded to a 128-row multiple, so 1-3-row decode segments never touch the example's unexercised non-16-multiple group path; the cost is honest — ~200 nonzero groups x 128 rows for ~384 real rows, far more MMA work than the tokens require, and it still wins 3.9x (tighter granularity is future work, not this experiment). GATE STATUS, STATED PLAINLY: the local D13 TF pre-gate could NOT be run — GPUs 4-7 were held for this entire session by the worker's own exp-0016 benchmark (server pid 47423, 168-180 GiB/GPU) and GPUs 0-3 by the vLLM baseline, so a 4-GPU engine server did not fit the budget. That gate measures prefill (max_tokens=1), which arm a proves is bitwise unchanged from exp-0016's green run, and it does not exercise the decode path this patch changes at all. Untested in situ, the one place a surprise could live: graph-pool growth with the m_cap=32896-row transient buffers live in every captured segment across 4 devices (freed and reused within a capture; exp-0016 measured ~90 GiB headroom). No new JIT compiles — decode reuses prefill's (device, K, N) kernel-cache keys, so the ~33 s first-request compile storm does not grow.
predicted_delta: +100-140% timeboxed decode_heavy tok/s: 185-225 vs the best same-protocol accepted row 93.0 (merge bar 93.3; higher if exp-0016 lands first, and this spec's base already contains exp-0016's mechanism so it should clear whatever exp-0016 sets). Cycle model on the 64-seq/8192-tok cohort: the 3.90x graphed-layer ratio applied to exp-0012's in-situ table takes the routed-expert term 266.4 -> ~68 ms and the decode step 322.7 -> ~125 ms, so the 30.4 s decode term -> ~11.8 s; with exp-0016's W4A4 prefill term of 22-25 s the cohort is ~35-39 s -> 210-234 tok/s, discounted ~5% for the one-time compile+repack storm inside the 600 s timebox -> 185-225. Downside case if the graphed decode does not realize the isolated ratio (routing concentration, memory pressure, or the padded-group waste biting harder in situ): a result near exp-0016's own 125-150, which would still clear the 93.3 bar and would itself be the measurement that separates the two halves. prefill_heavy rides the unchanged prefill path.
